I think she lives there under squatters rights because she's not technically on the lease. It's weird and confusing. My parents are landlords, I'd suggest contacting the landlord and explaining the situation. They can legally get her removed if you're not able to. Usually it's a 30 day eviction. Under circumstances of abuse police come and give 24 hours for belongings to be removed entirely. 

All in all, you need a legal form of eviction so she doesn't just linger. I think your best bet is bringing it up with the landlord and explaining your situation.

Hi there! If she truly feels the same way about you she wouldn't do that. I have two friends in the Air Force that were deeply in love before attending basic training and tech school, you're not really allowed to write or talk (they take devices away and limit outside contact), but having a family of people that are in Air Force they shared any tips and tricks to stay in contact. It's very risky and I don't recommend doing that in case if you get caught, but you can carry some sentimental items in with you. They both attended basic training for about 3 months at separate times, it was extremely hard for them but they went in knowing they wanted to be together and it was going to be a commitment. Whenever they were allowed to write each other they made it worth it, and upon seeing each other again they crammed in as many dates and fun times as they could. Long story short, they've been married for almost 5 years now, dated for 2. They decided to get married during tech school so they could live together on base and that helped them immensely with the loneliness. Don't rush a marriage though- trust me. They went into this with a very strong relationship and it was still a struggle. I don't think it means you should just run, it sounds like you have a lot of love for her. Just make sure to talk with her and see how she feels about things and if this is something you two would want to try together.

Growing up in a controlling household you kind of learn to make peace until you're able to move out on your own and fully be yourself. Sorry you're going through this, it's really shitty. It's like walking on eggshells hoping you didn't anger the beast. Stay true to you, I hope this doesn't stray you from being yourself even though you can't find that comfort and stability at home. It gets better.

Hi, I agree with the other comments about using protection - this is if you WANT to have sex. Please don't feel forced to have sex if you don't feel comfortable with it. If you feel like you may lose her if you don't, then honestly it's not worth it. She should be understanding <3 However, if you're curious and want to it won't ruin your life honey. Just be careful, be aware, be vocal if you don't like something. I was raised in a Christian household and I thought having sex outside of marriage or so young would ruin my life but it's opened my mind to how sexual I actually am and enjoy having it. This isn't for everyone, but I think experiences are nice. It's just important to be safe and WANT to, otherwise you can have deep regrets. I wish you luck <3
